authors: Thomas D. O'Sullivan, Norman O. Smith, Bartholomew Nagy
title: Solubility of natural gases in aqueous salt solutions-III. Nitrogen in aqueous NaCl at high pressures
experimental_method: One-gallon stirred stainless-steel autoclave equilibrated about 8 h under N2 (pumped with water); liquid samples of 20-25 ml withdrawn into a calibrated gas burette (Wiebe-type) and gas volume and residual liquid measured.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature held to +-0.5 C (brief excursions +-2 C); pressure +-0.5 atm at 100 atm and +-1 atm at 600 atm (Heise gauge); successive samples deviated on average about 0.5 per cent.
quality_remarks: Preliminary measurements. Pressures in Table 2 are total pressures with no water-vapour correction; the authors say the Wiebe et al. partial-pressure corrections at 102.5 C were probably underestimated. Table 1 agreement with Wiebe et al. (1933) is stated as good. Text layer of the PDF is badly garbled (e.g. '6X@', '2&B', '1s.0'); all values read from the page image. Salt-free vs total basis of mole fraction not stated. The 102.5 C Wiebe values quoted in the text (not in a table) are not extracted.
